workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§245–245
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §245: The Fall of Teb-Tenggeri
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§245–245, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Teb-Tenggeri, the shaman son of Münlig, draws the peoples of the nine tongues to himself and beats the envoy Soqor whom Ödchigin sends to claim back his people. Ödchigin goes in person and is made to kneel by the Qongqotan; he weeps at the Qahan’s bed, and Börte-Üjin, sitting up beside him, asks the Qahan how he can look on. Then, when Father Münlig comes with his seven sons, Teb-Tenggeri among them, Ödchigin seizes Teb-Tenggeri by the collar, and the three wrestlers waiting outside break his back. Grammar to watch: the dative-locatives that the Ming glossators write 行, the long converb chains in -žu/-žü, the reflexive-possessives -ben/-jen/-γ̇an, and the quotations, where Shiratori’s marks are partial and the notes say where `i` supplies one.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Teġün-ü qoina jesün keleten irgen Teb-Teṅgeri-dür qurižu

words.reading: 帖卜-驣格舌理-突︀舌兒 Teb-Teṅgeri-dür

sentences.l: That-of after nine tongue-having people Teb-Tenggeri-at gathering,
sentences.i: After that, the people of the nine tongues gathered to Teb-Tenggeri,
sentences.n: Read keleten as kele ‘tongue’ + the possessive plural -ten (Ming 言語有的每), so jesün keleten irgen is ‘the nine-tongued people’, a way of saying all the peoples; jesün stays ‘nine’. Teġün-ü qoina is ‘after that’ (the stem teġün- before a case ending). Teb-Teṅgeri-dür is a name with the dative-locative -dür (Ming 行), ‘to, at Teb-Tenggeri’; qurižu ‘gathering’ is a converb that waits for bolba in the next unit. This opens §245 and Shiratori’s sentence runs to bolba; I cut it in two at the converb.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-u kirüġe-dēče olon Teb-Teṅgeri- dür quriqun bolba.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
gathering-place of horses? (sense from the Ming; stem uncertain) [聚馬處]
ablative: from, than (long vowel; front-vowel form)
Teb-Tenggeri, a shaman's name (the word is cut at the line end and finished by dür) [巫名]
dative-locative: at, to (the end of Teb-Teṅgeri-dür) [行]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan-of kirüge-from many Teb-Tenggeri-at gathering-ones became.
sentences.i: More gathered to Teb-Tenggeri than at Chinggis Qahan’s horse-gathering place.
sentences.n: The pivot is the ablative -dēče on kirüġe, which I read as comparative, ‘from / than’. kirüġe is glossed 聚馬處 ‘place where horses are gathered’; the stem is uncertain and I follow the Ming. quriqun (Ming 聚每) is quri- ‘gather’ + a plural ending, ‘those who gather’, and olon ‘many’ before it makes ‘the gatherers became many’ (bolba, Ming 做了). Teb-Teṅgeri- and dür are one word that Shiratori breaks at the line end (words 11–12). The comparison is my reading of the ablative and may be too strong.

sentences.t: Tein quriqui-dur Temüge- Ödčigin-(n)e qarijatan irgen Teb-Teṅgeri-dür odčuγ̇ui.

words.reading: 中忽舌里中灰-突︀舌兒 quriqui-dur

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at the time of, when
Temüge, a man's name (the first half of the double name Temüge-Ödčigin) [人名]
dependents, those attached to a man (formation uncertain) [屬的每]

words.reading: 帖卜-驣格舌理-突︀舌兒 Teb-Teṅgeri-dür

sentences.l: So gathering-at, Temüge-Ödčigin-to dependent people Teb-Tenggeri-at went.
sentences.i: While they were gathering in this way, the people who belonged to Temüge-Ödchigin went over to Teb-Tenggeri.
sentences.n: quriqui-dur is the participle -qui + -dur, ‘at the gathering, when gathering’ (Ming 聚時). Temüge- and Ödčigin-(n)e are the two halves of one double name, Temüge-Ödčigin, broken at the line end; the dative -(n)e on a name is Ming 行 and here means ‘of / belonging to’: qarijatan (Ming 屬的每 ‘those attached’) is the dependents, the people of his appanage. The form of qarijatan is uncertain; the Ming gives the sense. odčuγ̇ui is od- ‘go’ + a past ending I cannot analyse further.

sentences.t: Ödčigin nojan oduγsan irge-ben γuira Soqor neretü elči-jen iležüġüi.

morph.gloss: people (a form of irgen) [百姓 自的行]
to go and demand (reading uncertain: γu- ‘ask, demand’ + -ira; stem inferred from the Ming) [索去]
Soqor, a man's name (the word is also 'blind', but the Ming marks it as a name) [人名]

sentences.l: Ödčigin lord gone-ones people-his-own to-demand-back Soqor named envoy-his-own sent.
sentences.i: Ödchigin Noyan sent his envoy, a man named Soqor, to demand back his own people who had gone.
sentences.n: Read oduγsan (od- ‘go’ + the past participle) as ‘the gone ones’, qualifying irge-ben ‘his own people’ (-ben is the reflexive-possessive, Ming 自的行). γuira (Ming 索去) is ‘go and demand’; the stem is inferred from the Ming and the ending is uncertain. Soqor neretü is ‘named Soqor’ (nere ‘name’ + -tü ‘having’); the Ming marks Soqor 人名, a name, though the same spelling elsewhere means ‘blind’. elči-jen is ‘his own envoy’; iležüġüi ‘sent’ (past ending uncertain).

sentences.t: Teb-Teṅgeri Soqor elči-de ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Soqor, a man's name (the word is also 'blind', but the Ming marks it as a name) [人名]

sentences.l: Teb-Tenggeri Soqor envoy-to, saying:
sentences.i: Teb-Tenggeri said to Soqor the envoy:
sentences.n: Teb-Teṅgeri is the subject, elči-de the envoy as recipient (dative -de, Ming 行), and ügülerün the converb ‘saying’ with its colon: the speech follows. Shiratori’s opening quotation mark falls on the next word, Ödčigin.

sentences.t: "Ödčigin ta žirin elčiten bolžuγ̇ui. keġežü
sentences.l: "Ödčigin, you two envoy-having have-become, saying
sentences.i: “Ödchigin, you two have become envoys,” he said,
sentences.n: The Ming reads 人名 您 兩箇 使臣有的每 做了有 ‘Ödchigin, you two have become envoys’. The sense is uncertain: whether Teb-Tenggeri mocks Ödchigin and his man, or Ödchigin is named in the third person, the Mongol does not say. elčiten is elči + -ten, ‘those having envoys / envoys’; ta is ‘you’, polite plural (Ming 您). Shiratori opens a quotation at Ödčigin and prints no close before keġežü; `i` supplies the closing mark after bolžuγ̇ui. keġežü ‘saying’ is a converb that ties the speech to the beating in the next unit.

sentences.l: Soqor envoy-ACC his beating, walking saddle his carrying-on-back, made-return.
sentences.i: He beat Soqor, Ödchigin’s envoy, and sent him back on foot with his saddle on his back.
sentences.n: A converb chain: asigižu ‘beating’ (stem inferred from Ming 打), jabuγan ‘walking’ (Ming 步行), ürgežü ‘carrying on the back’ (Ming 敎背着), all waiting for the final verb qariγ̇ulžuγ̇ui, qari- ‘return’ + the causative -γ̇ul- + a past ending: ‘made him go back’ (Ming 敎囘去了有). elči-ji is the accusative (Ming 行). The first in-ü ‘his’ I take as Ödchigin’s (it follows ‘envoy’), the second as Soqor’s (after ‘saddle’); the Ming gives 他的 both times and does not settle this.

sentences.t: Ödčigin Soqor elči-jen asigižu jabuγan iregdežü

morph.gloss: Soqor, a man's name (the word is also 'blind', but the Ming marks it as a name) [人名]
to beat (stem inferred from the Ming 打 ‘strike’) [打着]
to walk, go on foot [步行]

sentences.l: Ödčigin, Soqor envoy-his-own beating, walking, was-come-to.
sentences.i: Soqor, his envoy, came back to Ödchigin on foot, beaten.
sentences.n: iregdežü is ire- ‘come’ + the passive -gde- + the converb -žü (Ming 被來着 ‘being come to’): the passive turns ‘Soqor came to him’ into ‘he was come to’, which is why Ödchigin has no case ending here but is the one received. The two converbs asigižu and jabuγan repeat the previous unit’s words and now describe Soqor’s return.

sentences.t: manaγar-ši Ödčigin öġesün Teb-Teṅgeri-dür odču ügülerün:

words.reading: 帖卜騰格舌理-突︀舌兒 Teb-Teṅgeri-dür

sentences.l: Tomorrow-toward Ödčigin himself Teb-Tenggeri-at going, saying:
sentences.i: The next morning Ödchigin went himself to Teb-Tenggeri and said:
sentences.n: manaγar-ši is manaγar ‘tomorrow’ + the directive -ši ‘toward’ (Ming 明早), here ‘the next morning’ because the narration is in the past. öġesün is ‘himself’ (Ming 自己); odču ‘going’ is a converb leading to ügülerün ‘saying:’, whose colon opens a speech. The opening mark Shiratori prints on the next unit is Soqor.

sentences.t: "Soqor elči-jen ileġesü asigižu jabuγan iležüġü.

morph.gloss: Soqor, a man's name (the word is also 'blind', but the Ming marks it as a name) [人名]
to beat (stem inferred from the Ming 打 ‘strike’) [打着]
to walk, go on foot [步行]

sentences.l: "Soqor envoy-my-own if-sent, beating, walking, sent.
sentences.i: “When I sent my envoy Soqor, you beat him and sent him back on foot.
sentences.n: ileġesü (Ming 敎來呵) is ile- ‘send’ + the conditional -ġesü, ‘if / when I sent’; the pair of converbs asigižu, jabuγan then lead to iležüġü ‘sent (him back)’ (Ming 敎來了). The subject of iležüġü, left unstated, is Teb-Tenggeri. I give ‘sent back’ because the Ming says ‘made (him) come’; the glossary notes that iležüġü is not firm. Shiratori’s opening quotation mark, the first of Ödčigin’s speech, sits on Soqor; the mark is not closed until irebe in the next unit.

sentences.t: Edöġe bi irge-ben γuira irebe"

morph.gloss: people (a form of irgen) [百姓 自的行]
to go and demand (reading uncertain: γu- ‘ask, demand’ + -ira; stem inferred from the Ming) [索]

sentences.l: Now I people-my-own to-demand came"
sentences.i: Now I have come to demand my own people.”
sentences.n: γuira is the same ‘go and demand’ as above; irge-ben ‘my own people’ (the reflexive -ben takes the speaker). bi is the pronoun ‘I’; irebe ‘came’ (Ming 來了) ends the speech, so Shiratori’s closing mark sits on it.

sentences.t: keġegdežü doloγ̇an Qoṅγotan Ödčigin-i endēče tendēče qaγ̇ažu

morph.gloss: the Qongqotan, a clan name [種(名)]
to surround, enclose (stem inferred from the Ming 圍) [圍着]

sentences.l: Being-told, seven Qongqotan Ödčigin-ACC from-here from-there surrounding
sentences.i: At these words the seven Qongqotan closed in on Ödchigin from this side and from that,
sentences.n: keġegdežü is keġe- ‘say’ + the passive -gde- + -žü, ‘being told’ (Ming 被說着): the speech just made is the cause. Qoṅγotan is a clan or people (Ming 種名) and I keep Shiratori’s plural-looking form as the name; doloγ̇an ‘seven’ counts them. endēče tendēče, ‘from here, from there’, are ene/tende + the long ablative -ēče; qaγ̇ažu is ‘surrounding’ (stem inferred from Ming 圍着). The sentence goes on to the next unit.

sentences.t: "Soqor elči-jen ilekü čin-u žöb bi" keġežü

morph.gloss: Soqor, a man's name (the word is also 'blind', but the Ming marks it as a name) [人名]

sentences.l: "Soqor envoy-your-own sending, your right is," saying
sentences.i: “Your sending of your envoy Soqor — that is right,” they said,
sentences.n: The Ming reads 使臣自的行 敎來的 你的 是 有 ‘the sending of your envoy is yours, right’. I give the plain sense and do not guess the tone: it may be ironic, a taunt before they threaten him, since Ödchigin answers by admitting a fault. bi here is the verb ‘is’ (Ming 有), not the pronoun. čin-u is ‘your’ (čin- is the oblique stem of či). Opening mark Shiratori’s, at Soqor; the closing mark sits on bi, and keġežü ‘saying’ follows it.

sentences.t: bariqu-ača tusqu-ača kigderün ajužu Ödčigin nojan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: to strike (stem inferred from the Ming 打; uncertain) [要打]

sentences.l: Seizing-from, striking-from when-being-made, fearing, Ödčigin lord saying:
sentences.i: When they were about to seize and beat him, Ödchigin Noyan took fright and said:
sentences.n: bariqu-ača and tusqu-ača are the participles ‘seizing’ and ‘striking’ with the ablative -ača (Ming 要拿, 要打, ‘about to seize, about to strike’); kigderün is ki- ‘do, make’ + the passive -gde- + -rün, ‘when being made (to be)’ (Ming 被做時). I take the whole as ‘when it came to seizing and striking’. ajužu is ‘fearing’ (Ming 怕著).

sentences.t: "Elči ilekü min-uγ̇ai buruγ̇u" keġežüġü.

morph.gloss: my, of me (genitive stem of bi) [我的]
ending uncertain (the Ming 我的 gives nothing for it)
wrong, a fault (sense from the Ming 不是了 ‘was wrong’) [不是了]

sentences.l: "Envoy sending mine wrong," said.
sentences.i: “Sending an envoy was my fault,” he said.
sentences.n: buruγ̇u is glossed 不是了 ‘was not right, was wrong’ here and 不是 ‘not right’ a few lines on; the glossary carries the word as uncertain because of an unreadable Ming character elsewhere, but these two Ming glosses make ‘wrong, a fault’ safe. min-uγ̇ai is min-u ‘my’ with an ending -γ̇ai I cannot explain (Ming 我的). keġežüġü is ‘said’ (past narrative; Ming 說有). Shiratori’s opening mark sits on Elči and his closing mark on buruγ̇u.

sentences.t: Doloγ̇an Qoṅγotan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: the Qongqotan, a clan name [種(名)]

sentences.l: Seven Qongqotan saying:
sentences.i: The seven Qongqotan said:
sentences.n: Another colon introduces the next speech; Doloγ̇an is capitalised only because it begins a sentence.

to repent, make amends (Ming 悔過) [悔︀過]

sentences.l: "Wrong if-be, repenting, kneel," saying
sentences.i: “If it is wrong, repent and kneel,” they said,
sentences.n: böġesü is bü- ‘be’ + the conditional -ġesü (Ming 有呵), so ‘if it is a fault’. namančilan (Ming 悔過) is namančila- ‘repent, make amends’ + the converb -n; I do not know the stem outside the Ming. šögöd, ‘kneel’, has a stem šögö- inferred from Ming 跪 and an ending -d that I cannot explain; I read it as an imperative from the sense. Opening mark Shiratori’s on Buruγ̇u; closing mark on šögöd.

sentences.t: Teb-Teṅgeri-jin qoināča šögöd- gežüġüi.

morph.gloss: to kneel (stem inferred from the Ming 跪) [跪了]
ending unexplained (the word is cut at the line end and finished by gežüġüi)
causative(?): make … (compare sögödgeġüldebe, Ming 敎跪) [有]

sentences.l: Teb-Tenggeri-of from-behind kneel- made.
sentences.i: and they made Ödchigin kneel behind Teb-Tenggeri.
sentences.n: šögöd- and gežüġüi are one word broken at the line end (words 110–111): šögöd-ge-žüġüi. The -ge- I read as a causative (compare sögödgeġüldebe, Ming 敎跪, a few lines on), though the Ming here says 跪了有 ‘knelt’ without 敎. The subject and the person made to kneel are not named in this unit; from Ödchigin’s complaint two units on they are the Qongqotan and Ödchigin. qoināča is qoina ‘behind’ + the short ablative -ča (Ming 自後).

sentences.t: irge-ben ba ese ögtežü

morph.gloss: people (a form of irgen) [百姓 自的行]

sentences.l: People-his-own also not having-been-given,
sentences.i: His people had not been handed over to him either,
sentences.n: ögtežü is ög- ‘give’ + -te- + -žü, a passive-looking converb (Ming 被與着 ‘having been given’), the same -te- that the 242–244 notes read in ögtekün. ba is ‘also’ (Ming 也) and ese ‘not’ (the negative of a past action). irge-ben is ‘his own people’, as before.

sentences.t: Ödčigin manaγar-ši erte Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-i bosuγ̇ai üdüġüj-e oron dotora büküi-dür

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
accusative (here marking the subject of a time clause; Ming 行)
bed, bedding (the same spelling as oro- ‘to enter’) [被窠]

sentences.l: Ödčigin tomorrow-toward early Chinggis Qaγan-ACC rising not-yet-at bed within being-at,
sentences.i: Ödchigin, early the next morning, before Chinggis Qahan had risen, while he was still lying in his bed,
sentences.n: The time clause is bosuγ̇ai üdüġüj-e: üdüġüi ‘not yet’ (Ming 未) + the dative-locative -e, ‘at the not-yet’, with bosuγ̇ai ‘rising’; the ending -γ̇ai I cannot analyse. The Qahan stands in the accusative -i (Ming 行) as the subject of this clause. oron is the noun ‘bed’ here (Ming 被窠), not the verb ‘enter’; oron dotora ‘inside the bed’. büküi-dür is bü- ‘be’ + -küi + -dür, ‘at the being, while he was’ (Ming 有時).

morph.gloss: to kneel (stem inferred from the Ming 跪) [跪着]

sentences.l: Entering, having wept, kneeling, saying:
sentences.i: went in, wept, knelt, and said:
sentences.n: Three converbs in a row, orožu ‘entering’, uilaγ̇ad ‘having wept’ (uila- ‘weep’ + -γ̇ad), sögödčü ‘kneeling’ (stem inferred from Ming 跪; the d is unexplained), then ügülerün. The subject, Ödchigin, is carried over from the previous unit.

sentences.l: I myself to-demand if-go, seven Qongqotan-by from-here from-there surrounding
sentences.i: When I went to demand them myself, the seven Qongqotan closed in on me from this side and from that,
sentences.n: oduγ̇asu is od- ‘go’ + -uγ̇asu, a conditional (Ming 去呵 ‘if / when I go’). Qoṅγotan-a carries the dative-locative -a in the sense ‘by the Qongqotan’, the agent of the action: I follow the glossary for this form. endēče tendēče qaγ̇ažu repeats the surrounding of the narration.

sentences.t: namančilaγ̇ulžu Teb-Teṅgeri-jin qoināča sögödgeġüldebe"

morph.gloss: to repent, make amends (Ming 悔過) [敎悔︀過着]

words.reading: 莎葛惕客兀勒迭罷 sögödgeġüldebe

morph.gloss: to kneel (stem inferred from the Ming 跪) [敎跪了]
(past ending -be after the causative; reading uncertain)

sentences.l: Making-repent, Teb-Tenggeri-of from-behind, they-made-kneel-me"
sentences.i: made me repent, and made me kneel behind Teb-Tenggeri,”
sentences.n: namančilaγ̇ulžu is namančila- ‘repent’ + the causative -γ̇ul- + -žu, ‘making (me) repent’ (Ming 敎悔過着); sögödgeġüldebe is the kneeling verb with -ge- and the causative -ġül- (Ming 敎跪了): ‘made me kneel’. The ending -de- before -be I cannot explain; I read the whole as a plain past. The closing mark is Shiratori’s, on sögödgeġüldebe.

sentences.t: kēġed uilaba.

morph.gloss: converb: having said (run together and written with ē)

sentences.l: Having said, wept.
sentences.i: Having said this, he wept.
sentences.n: kēġed is keġe- ‘say’ + the converb -ġed, written with a long ē (the stem and ending run together); uilaba is uila- ‘weep’ + the past -ba. The subject, Ödchigin, is carried over.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-i doṅγoduγ̇ai üdüġüj-e

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
accusative (here marking the subject of a time clause; Ming 行)
to sound, make a noise (Ming 作聲) [作聲]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan-ACC sounding not-yet-at,
sentences.i: Before Chinggis Qahan had made a sound,
sentences.n: The same time clause as before: the Qahan in the accusative (Ming 行) and ‘not yet’ (üdüġüj-e), here with doṅγoduγ̇ai (Ming 作聲 ‘make a noise’; the ending -duγ̇ai I take as the counterpart of bosuγ̇ai above). The sense is that Börte-Üjin moved before the Qahan woke or spoke; that is a reading of the Ming.

sentences.t: Börte-Üžin oron dotora öṅdeižü saγ̇užu künžile-ijen žaqa-bar ebčeġü-ben tüidčü

morph.gloss: Börte-Üjin, a woman's name (one two-part name) [夫人名]
bed, bedding (the same spelling as oro- ‘to enter’) [被窠]
to rise up, stretch up (Ming 伸起) [伸起着]
quilt, coverlet (Ming 被兒) [被兒(自)的(行)]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form, with a linking i)
chest, breast (short form before the reflexive) [胷 自的行]
to cover, screen (stem inferred from the Ming 遮) [遮着]

sentences.l: Börte-Üžin bed within stretching-up, sitting, coverlet-her-own edge-with chest-her-own covering,
sentences.i: Börte-Üjin sat up inside the bed, covering her own breast with the edge of her quilt,
sentences.n: öṅdeižü (Ming 伸起着 ‘stretching up’) is a verb whose stem I cannot place, here ‘sitting up’ (l keeps the Ming’s ‘stretching up’); saγ̇užu ‘sitting’. künžile-ijen is ‘her own quilt’ (Ming 被兒自的行) with the linking i of the reflexive -ijen after a vowel stem. žaqa-bar is žaqa ‘edge / collar’ + the instrumental -bar, ‘with the edge’; the Ming 領敎 is odd, and I give the common sense. ebčeġü-ben is ‘her own chest’; tüidčü ‘covering’ (stem inferred from Ming 遮着). Börte-Üžin is one two-part woman’s name.

sentences.t: Ödčigin-ü uilaqu-ji üžežü nilbusu aldaγ̇ad ügülerün:
sentences.l: Ödčigin-of weeping-ACC seeing, tear let-fall, saying:
sentences.i: seeing Ödchigin weeping, she let her tears fall and said:
sentences.n: uilaqu-ji is uila- ‘weep’ + the participle -qu + the accusative -ji, ‘the weeping (of Ödchigin)’; Ödčigin-ü is his name in the genitive (Ming 人名的). aldaγ̇ad is alda- ‘let fall, drop’ with the converb -γ̇ad (Ming 墮了). The subject is Börte-Üjin.

sentences.t: "Jakigsed Qoṅγotan tede öčigen Qasar-i ömörežü žančižu kü büleġei.

morph.gloss: to do what? (Ming 做甚麽; stem uncertain) [做甚麽來的(每)]
the Qongqotan, a clan name [種(名)]
to band together, take sides (stem inferred from the Ming 黨) [黨着]
past: there was, used to be

sentences.l: "What-did-ones Qongqotan those the-other-day Qasar-ACC banding-together, striking indeed were.
sentences.i: “What have they been doing, these Qongqotan? Only the other day they ganged up on Qasar and beat him.
sentences.n: Jakigsed (Ming 做甚麽來的 ‘what have they done’) is a plural participle from a stem jaki- that I take as ‘do what’; the form is uncertain, and I make it a question with tede ‘those’. öčigen is ‘the other day, lately’ (Ming 昨前). ömörežü, ‘banding together’ (Ming 黨着), and žančižu, ‘striking’ (Ming 打着), are converbs before büleġei, bü- ‘be’ + the past -leġei (Ming 有來), with kü ‘indeed’ (Ming 也). Qasar-i is the accusative (Ming 行); §244 has Qasar accused and bound, which is the event alluded to. Shiratori’s opening mark sits on Jakigsed.

sentences.t: Edöġe basa ene Ödčigin-i jakin qoināča-γ̇an sögödgemüi.

morph.gloss: to kneel (stem inferred from the Ming 跪) [敎跪有]

sentences.l: Now again this Ödčigin-ACC why from-behind-own makes-kneel.
sentences.i: Now, once more, why do they make Ödchigin kneel behind them?
sentences.n: basa is ‘again’ (Ming 再), jakin ‘why’; sögödgemüi is the kneeling verb, with the causative -ge- and the present -müi (Ming 敎跪有). qoināča-γ̇an is ‘from behind, one’s own’ (Ming 自後自的行): the reflexive -γ̇an points back at the subject, so ‘behind themselves’, which I render ‘behind them’.

sentences.t: ambar josun bolumui.

morph.gloss: what (sense from the Ming 甚麽; uncertain) [甚麽]
custom, reason, the right way [道理]

sentences.l: What custom is.
sentences.i: By what right is this done?
sentences.n: ambar (Ming 甚麽) ‘what’ is a word the glossary marks as uncertain; josun is ‘custom, right way’ (Ming 道理), and bolumui is bol- ‘become, be’ + the present -umui (Ming 做有). I give ‘by what right is this done’, which is the Ming’s sense, ‘what principle is it’.

sentences.t: Bel ede čigöd narad metüs deġü-ner-i čin-u ein oisulaldumui.

morph.gloss: to harm in secret, plot against (Ming 陰害) [陰害有]

sentences.l: Moreover these cypress-and-pine like younger-brothers-ACC your thus they-harm-in-secret.
sentences.i: Moreover, in this way they are plotting harm against these brothers of yours, who are like cypresses and pines.
sentences.n: čigöd narad are ‘cypresses, pines’ (Ming 檜每 松每), plural nouns; metüs ‘like’ + the plural -s (Ming 般每) makes ‘the likes of cypress and pine’, and ede ‘these’ qualifies the brothers: ‘these brothers of yours, cypress- and pine-like’. oisulaldumui is oisula- ‘harm secretly’ (Ming 陰害) + -ldu-, which I read as a reciprocal or collective, + the present -mui. The subject is not named; I supply ‘they’ for the Qongqotan. Bel is Ming 且 ‘moreover’.

sentences.t: Ünen ber mönö qoina neġüle metü beje čin-u negüs oduγ̇asu

morph.gloss: old tree (Ming 古樹; word uncertain) [古樹]
fall, collapse (Ming 倒; formation uncertain) [倒]

sentences.l: True indeed long-after old-tree like body your fallen if-it-goes,
sentences.i: Truly, in time to come, if your body falls like an old tree,
sentences.n: Ünen ber (Ming 實 也) is ‘truly’; mönö qoina is ‘from now on, hereafter’ (Ming 久後). neġüle is read from Ming 古樹 ‘old tree’; the word is uncertain, though the simile with a falling body suits it. negüs is glossed 倒 ‘fall’; oduγ̇asu ‘if it goes’ (od- ‘go’ + conditional) is the auxiliary, ‘if it goes to falling’, (the Ming has 倒 做呵 here and 倒 去呵 two units on).

sentences.t: nedkel metü ulus čin-u ken-e medeġülkün.

morph.gloss: ending of a command or question (uncertain)

sentences.l: Tangled-hemp like people your whom-to let-manage?
sentences.i: who will you have govern your people, who are like tangled hemp?
sentences.n: nedkel (Ming 亂麻) is ‘tangled hemp’ and ulus the people. ken-e is ken ‘who’ + the dative -e, ‘to whom’, and medeġülkün is mede- ‘manage, rule’ + the causative -ġül- + an ending -kün which I read as a question or a command (the Ming gives only 敎管). Börte is asking Chinggis whom he will have rule.

sentences.t: Tede tulu metü beje čin-u tulbas oduγ̇asu

morph.gloss: pillar-foot, base of a pillar (Ming 柱腳; word uncertain) [柱腳]
fall, overturn (Ming 倒; formation uncertain) [倒]

sentences.l: Those pillar-foot like body your overturned if-it-goes,
sentences.i: And if your body falls like the foot of a pillar,
sentences.n: Tede (Ming 他每 ‘those’) stands at the head of this clause and I cannot fit it into the grammar; I leave it out of `i` and read the clause as a second simile parallel to the old tree. tulu (Ming 柱腳 ‘foot of a pillar’) and tulbas (Ming 倒 ‘fall’) are both uncertain words, read from the Ming.

sentences.t: tujal metü ulus čin-u ken-e medeġülkün.

morph.gloss: flock of birds (Ming 羣鳥; word uncertain) [羣鳥]
ending of a command or question (uncertain)

sentences.l: Flock-of-birds like people your whom-to let-manage?
sentences.i: who will you have govern your people, who are like a flock of birds?
sentences.n: tujal is read from Ming 羣鳥 ‘a flock of birds’; the second half of the pair repeats the question as above.

sentences.t: Tede čigöd narad metü deġü-ner-i čin-u ein oisuladqun haran

morph.gloss: to harm in secret (Ming 陰害) [陰害的]

sentences.l: Those cypress-and-pine like younger-brothers-ACC your thus harm-plotting people
sentences.i: And those people who thus plot harm against your brothers, who are like cypresses and pines —
sentences.n: oisuladqun is oisula- ‘harm secretly’ + the plural participle -dqun, ‘those who harm’ (Ming 陰害的), here before haran ‘people / men’. The sentence is not finished in this unit and the predicate comes in the next one; my splitting of the pair into two units is for reading, not Shiratori’s.

sentences.t: min-u γurban dörben üčüged maγ̇un mandutala min-u jaγ̇u medeġülkün.

morph.gloss: my, of me (genitive of bi, set after its noun) [我的]
to grow up, thrive (Ming 長進; stem uncertain) [長進間]
my, of me (genitive of bi, set after its noun) [我的]
ending of a command or question (uncertain)

sentences.l: My three four small ones bad until-growing mine what let-manage.
sentences.i: while my three or four little ones are small and bad and still growing up, how shall mine be governed?
sentences.n: Börte speaks of her sons. γurban dörben is ‘three, four’ (about four sons, Ming 三四); üčüged is üčüge ‘small’ + the plural -d (Ming 小每); maγ̇un is ‘bad’ (Ming 歹), kept as the Ming has it; said of children it may mean ‘poor, weak’, but the text does not say, and mandutala ‘until / while growing’ (Ming 長進間; stem uncertain). min-u appears twice, ‘my’, and medeġülkün ‘let manage’ completes it as above. The Mongol is compressed and the sense is reconstructed from the Ming 我的 如何 敎管.

sentences.t: Tede jakigsed Qoṅγotan büleġe.

morph.gloss: to do what? (Ming 做甚麽; stem uncertain) [做甚來的(每)]
the Qongqotan, a clan name [種(名)]
past: there was, used to be

sentences.l: Those what-did-ones Qongqotan were.
sentences.i: What had they been doing, those Qongqotan?
sentences.n: The same unclear jakigsed (‘what have they done’) as before, now with büleġe ‘there was’ (Ming 有來), and with Qoṅγotan as the clan. I make it a rhetorical question to match the earlier one.

sentences.t: Tede deġü-ner(i)-jen teden-e tein kiġülžü
sentences.l: Those younger-brothers-own, to-them thus making-do,
sentences.i: As for those men, you have your own brothers made to act so before them —
sentences.n: Everything here is uncertain. teden-e is ‘to them’ (Ming 他每行); kiġülžü is ki- ‘do’ + the causative -ġül- + -žü, ‘making (someone) do’ (Ming 敎做着); deġü-ner(i)-jen is ‘one’s own younger brothers’ with the bracketed i of the accusative and the reflexive -jen (it refers back to the subject, či ‘you’). I read: you are letting your brothers be made to act (kneel) thus before them. The Ming does not settle it.

sentences.t: ker üžežü amu či" keġeġed
sentences.l: How seeing are you," having-said
sentences.i: how can you be looking on?” she said.
sentences.n: ker is ‘how’ (Ming 怎), üžežü ‘seeing’, amu ‘is’ (Ming 有) and či ‘you’: a question to Chinggis. keġeġed is ‘having said’ (the converb -ġed). Shiratori’s closing mark sits on či; his opening mark was at Jakigsed.

sentences.t: Börte-Üžin nibusun aldaba.

morph.gloss: Börte-Üjin, a woman's name (one two-part name) [夫人名]

sentences.l: Börte-Üžin tears let-fall.
sentences.i: Börte-Üjin shed tears.
sentences.n: nibusun is ‘tears’ (the longer form of nilbusu), and aldaba is alda- ‘let fall’ + the past -ba (Ming 墮了); the glossary elsewhere has alda- as ‘slip away’, so the sense is ‘let (tears) slip’.

sentences.t: Börte-Üžin-ü ene üge-dür Čiṅgis Qaγan Ödčigin-a ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Börte-Üjin, a woman's name [妻名 的]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.l: Börte-Üžin-of this word-in Chinggis Qaγan Ödčigin-to saying:
sentences.i: At these words of Börte-Üjin, Chinggis Qahan said to Ödchigin:
sentences.n: Börte-Üžin-ü is the genitive ‘of Börte-Üjin’; üge-dür is üge ‘word’ + -dür, ‘in the speech’. Ödčigin-a is the dative ‘to Ödchigin’ (back-vowel -a after a name). Qaγan is `l`’s form of the title; `i` writes Qahan. ügülerün with its colon opens the next speech.

sentences.t: "Teb-Teṅgeri edöġe irekü.
sentences.l: "Teb-Tenggeri now is-coming.
sentences.i: “Teb-Tenggeri is coming now.
sentences.n: irekü is ire- ‘come’ + the participle -kü (Ming 來有), a participle used as a verb, ‘is about to come, will come’. Shiratori’s opening quote sits on Teb-Teṅgeri.

sentences.t: Čidaqui-ača ker ba üileddüġesü či mede" keġebe.
sentences.l: Able-from how also if-you-do you know," said.
sentences.i: Do as you are able; however you set about it, you know.” So he said.
sentences.n: The least certain unit. Čidaqui-ača (Ming 能的行) is čida- ‘be able’ + the participle -qui + the ablative, which I take as ‘as far as you are able’; ker ba (Ming 怎生也) is ‘in whatever way’, üileddüġesü ‘if you do’ (Ming 做呵; stem üiled- plus an unexplained -dü-), mede the bare stem ‘know!’ (Ming 知). The colloquial Ming reads ‘as for one who is able, however you do it, you know’, i.e. do it your way. Closing mark Shiratori’s, on mede; keġebe ‘said’ (past -be).

sentences.t: Teġün-dür Ödčigin bosuγ̇ad nilbusu-γ̇an arčiγ̇ad γarču γurban bökös-i beledčü baiba.

morph.gloss: that (oblique stem of tere) [那的 裏]

sentences.l: That-at Ödčigin rising, tear-own wiping, going-out, three strong-men-ACC preparing stood.
sentences.i: At that, Ödchigin rose, wiped away his tears, went out, and having made three wrestlers ready, stood by.
sentences.n: A chain of converbs: bosuγ̇ad ‘having risen’, arčiγ̇ad ‘having wiped’ (stem inferred from Ming 拭), γarču ‘going out’, beledčü ‘preparing’, then baiba ‘stood’. nilbusu-γ̇an is ‘his own tears’ (the reflexive -γ̇an). bökös-i is the plural of bökö ‘wrestler, strong man’ with the accusative -i (Ming 力士每行). I read beledčü baiba as ‘stood, having made (them) ready’, i.e. he had the three men ready outside.

sentences.t: Qurumud atala Müṅlig ečige doloγ̇an köġüd-lüġe-ben irežü

morph.gloss: a short while (Ming 少時; word uncertain) [少時]

sentences.l: A-short-while being, Münlig father seven sons-with-own coming,
sentences.i: After a little while Father Münlig arrived with his seven sons,
sentences.n: Qurumud atala is Ming 少時 有間 ‘while a short time remained / passed’; atala is a- ‘be’ + -tala ‘while, until’, and qurumud is a word I know only from the Ming. köġüd-lüġe-ben is köġün ‘son’ + the plural -d + the comitative -lüġe + the reflexive -ben, ‘together with his own sons’ (Ming 兒子一同自的行). Müṅlig ečige is ‘Father Münlig’, as in the house name.

sentences.t: doloγ̇an büri orožu Teb-Teṅgeri tüsürge-jin baraγ̇un eteġed saγ̇udqui-luγ̇a

morph.gloss: banquet (Ming 酒局; sense uncertain) [酒局 的]

sentences.l: Seven all entering, Teb-Tenggeri banquet-of right side as-soon-as-sitting,
sentences.i: all seven came in, and as soon as they sat down on the right of Teb-Tenggeri’s banquet,
sentences.n: büri (Ming 全 ‘whole’) after doloγ̇an means ‘all seven’. tüsürge is Ming 酒局 ‘banquet, wine-office’ (the sense is uncertain) with the genitive -jin, ‘of the banquet’; the thing so named is Teb-Tenggeri’s. baraγ̇un eteġed is ‘right side’. saγ̇udqui-luγ̇a is saγ̇u- ‘sit’ + a participle + -luγ̇a, ‘at the moment of sitting’ (Ming 纔坐呵). Teb-Teṅgeri here has no case ending of its own.

sentences.t: Ödčigin Teb-Teṅgeri-jin žaqa in-ü barižu

morph.gloss: his, her (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to take hold of, seize [拿着]

sentences.l: Ödčigin Teb-Tenggeri-of collar him-of seizing,
sentences.i: Ödchigin seized Teb-Tenggeri by the collar,
sentences.n: žaqa is ‘collar, edge’ (Ming 衣領); in-ü ‘his’ follows it; barižu is ‘seizing’ (Ming 拿着). The speech that follows has no opening quotation mark in Shiratori; `i` supplies it at the next unit and says so there.

sentences.t: öčigen üdür nama-ji namančilan büleġe či. Sorilduja"

morph.gloss: to repent, make amends (Ming 悔過) [敎悔︀過]
past: there was, used to be
to try, test (Ming 試) [共試咱]

sentences.l: Yesterday day me-ACC repenting you-were. Let-us-try-one-another"
sentences.i: “Yesterday you made me repent. Let us try each other!”
sentences.n: öčigen üdür (Ming 昨 日) is ‘yesterday’; nama-ji is ‘me’ (accusative -ji), namančilan ‘repenting’ + büleġe ‘was’ is Ming 敎悔過 有來 ‘had (me) repent’, with či ‘you’. Sorilduja is sori- ‘try’ + the reciprocal -ldu- + the hortative -ja (Ming 共試咱), ‘let us try one another’. The opening quotation mark is `i` only, supplied here because Shiratori prints none; the closing mark is his, on Sorilduja.

sentences.t: keġežü žaqa in-ü barižu egüden žüg čirbe.

morph.gloss: his, her (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to take hold of, seize [拿着]

sentences.l: Saying, collar him-of seizing, door toward dragged.
sentences.i: and with that, gripping his collar, he dragged him toward the door.
sentences.n: keġežü is ‘saying’, žaqa in-ü barižu repeats the grip, egüden žüg is ‘toward the door’ (žüg ‘side, direction’ as a postposition), and čirbe is čir- ‘drag’ + the past -be (Ming 拖了).

sentences.t: Teb-Teṅgeri Ödčigin-ü esergü žaqa barižu barilduba.

morph.gloss: to take hold of, seize [拿着]

sentences.l: Teb-Tenggeri Ödčigin-of facing collar seizing, grappled.
sentences.i: Teb-Tenggeri seized Ödchigin’s collar in return, and they grappled.
sentences.n: esergü (Ming 迎着) is ‘facing, against’, i.e. in return; barilduba is bari- ‘seize’ + the reciprocal -ldu- + the past, ‘seized one another, grappled’ (Ming 相搏了).

sentences.t: Teb-Teṅgeri-jin maqalai barilduqui-dur qolumta teriġün-e unaba.

words.reading: 巴舌鄰勒都︀中灰-突︀舌兒 barilduqui-dur

glyphs.s: 巴舌鄰勒都︀中灰-突︀舌兒

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at the time of, when
fire-pan, hearth, brazier (Ming 火盤) [火盤]

sentences.l: Teb-Tenggeri-of cap grappling-at, fire-pan head-at fell.
sentences.i: As they grappled, Teb-Tenggeri’s cap fell at the head of the fire-pan.
sentences.n: maqalai is ‘cap’; barilduqui-dur is the grappling verb as a participle + -dur, ‘at the grappling, when they grappled’ (Ming 相搏時). qolumta is Ming 火盤 ‘fire-pan, brazier’, the hearth in the middle of the tent; teriġün-e is teriġün ‘head, top’ + the dative-locative -e, ‘at the head of’. unaba is una- ‘fall’ + the past.

sentences.t: Müṅlig ečige maqalai in-ü abču hünüsčü ebür-tür(i)-jen talbiba.

morph.gloss: his, her (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]

words.reading: 額不舌兒-禿舌里-顏 ebür-tür(i)-jen

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (front-vowel form, bracketed i)
to let go, set down [放了]

sentences.l: Münlig father cap him-of taking, smelling, lap-in-own put.
sentences.i: Father Münlig took up the cap, sniffed it, and put it in his own lap.
sentences.n: abču ‘taking’ and hünüsčü ‘smelling’ (Ming 嗅着) are converbs before talbiba ‘put, let go’ (past of talbi-); ebür-tür(i)-jen is ‘in one’s own lap’ with the bracketed linking i before the reflexive -jen. The reason for the sniffing is not given; the Ming gives only the actions.

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan said:
sentences.n: Qaγan is `l`’s form of the title; `i` writes Qahan. The colon opens a quotation whose opening mark Shiratori places on Γarču.

sentences.t: "Γarču bökö küčü temečeldüdkün" keġebe.

morph.gloss: to contend, vie (stem inferred from the Ming 爭) [相爭您]
element of the plural-address imperative (uncertain; compare soridqun)
imperative-optative ending of plural address (Ming 您)

sentences.l: "Going-out, strong-man strength let-you-vie," said.
sentences.i: “Go out, wrestlers, and vie in strength!” he said.
sentences.n: Γarču is γar- ‘go out’ + the converb -ču, here an order, ‘go out’; bökö is ‘strong man, wrestler’ (Ming 勇士), singular but addressed to both; küčü is ‘strength’ (Ming 氣力); temečeldüdkün is temeče- ‘vie’ (the glossary’s stem) + the reciprocal -ldü- + an unexplained -d- + the plural-address ending -kün (Ming 相爭您). The Qahan is sending the pair outside to settle it.

sentences.t: Ödčigin Teb-Teṅgeri-ji čirčü γarurun eġüden bosoγa žaγ̇ura

morph.gloss: converb of time: when going out

sentences.l: Ödčigin Teb-Tenggeri-ACC dragging, when-going-out door threshold at,
sentences.i: Ödchigin dragged Teb-Tenggeri out, and as they went out, at the threshold of the door,
sentences.n: čirčü is ‘dragging’ (čir-), γarurun ‘when going out’ (the converb -urun, Ming 出時); eġüden is the front-vowel variant of egüden ‘door’; bosoγa is ‘threshold’ (Ming 門限); žaγ̇ura is žaγ̇ur ‘middle, between’ + the dative-locative -a, ‘at / among’.

sentences.t: urida beledügsen γurban bökös esergü Teb-Teṅgeri-ji bariγ̇ad čirčü γarču
sentences.l: Formerly prepared three strong-men facing Teb-Tenggeri-ACC having-seized, dragging, going-out,
sentences.i: the three wrestlers who had been made ready beforehand met them, seized Teb-Tenggeri, dragged him out,
sentences.n: urida is ‘beforehand’; beledügsen is beled- ‘prepare’ + the past participle -ügsen, ‘prepared’ (Ming 准備了的). The three men are the bökös of the earlier unit. esergü ‘facing’ places them as meeting Teb-Tenggeri. bariγ̇ad ‘having seized’, čirčü ‘dragging’ and γarču ‘going out’ are converbs; the chain runs on through the next units to neġübe at the end of the section.

sentences.t: niruγ̇u in-ü quγulžü žeġün eteġed-ün terged-ün üžeġür-e örčü

morph.gloss: his, her (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
cart (terge- before the plural) [車每 的]
tip, end (Ming 捎頭) [捎 行]
to go (stem unknown; the Ming 去着 ‘going’ is all I have) [去着]

sentences.l: Back him-of breaking, left side-of carts-of tip-at going,
sentences.i: broke his back, and went to the tips of the carts on the left side,
sentences.n: quγulžü is quγul- ‘break’ + -žü (Ming 折折着 ‘breaking’), with niruγ̇u ‘spine’ (Ming 脊梁); the object is Teb-Tenggeri. žeġün eteġed-ün terged-ün is ‘of the left side, of the carts’, and üžeġür-e is üžeġür ‘tip, end’ (Ming 捎頭) with the dative-locative. örčü is ‘going’ (Ming 去着); the stem ör- I cannot place. The subject is the three strong men (and the Ming gives no verb for what was done to him there).

sentences.t: Ödčigin orožu ügülerün:
sentences.l: Ödčigin entering, saying:
sentences.i: Ödchigin went in and said:
sentences.n: Subject Ödchigin, converb orožu ‘entering’, then ügülerün: the colon opens his speech. Shiratori’s opening mark sits on the next word.

sentences.t: Teb-Teṅgeri nama-ji namančilan büleġe. Sorilduja kēġesü

morph.gloss: to repent, make amends (Ming 悔過) [敎悔︀過]
past: there was, used to be
to try, test (Ming 試) [共試咱]
conditional: when one says (written with ē)

sentences.l: "Teb-Tenggeri me-ACC repenting was. Let-us-try-one-another when-saying,
sentences.i: “Teb-Tenggeri made me repent. When I said, ‘Let us try each other,’
sentences.n: nama-ji namančilan büleġe is the same ‘had me repent’ as before; Sorilduja is again ‘let us try one another’, here with the conditional kēġesü ‘when / if one says’ (Ming 說呵), the ē being keġe- and -ġesü run together. Nested quotation: I set the inner saying in single marks in `i`; Shiratori marks only the outer opening.

sentences.t: ülü bolun arγalažu kebtemü.

morph.gloss: to scheme, put on a show of cleverness (Ming 使見識; stem uncertain) [使見識着]

sentences.l: Not consenting scheming lies.
sentences.i: he would not agree, but lay there scheming.
sentences.n: ülü bolun is ‘not being (willing)’, Ming 不 肯; ülü is the negative that goes with converbs and the present. arγalažu (Ming 使見識着 ‘showing off his wits’) is read from the Ming, the stem uncertain; kebtemü is kebte- ‘lie down’ + the present -mü (Ming 臥有). The speaker is describing how Teb-Tenggeri avoided a trial of strength.

sentences.t: Čaγtu nökör ažuγ̇u" kēġesü

morph.gloss: moderate, middling (Ming 酌中) [酌中有的]
conditional: when one says (written with ē)

sentences.l: Moderate companion he-was" when-saying
sentences.i: He was a middling companion.” When Ödchigin said this,
sentences.n: Čaγtu (Ming 酌中 ‘middling, moderate’) nökör (Ming 伴當 ‘companion’) ažuγ̇u (a- ‘be’ + the past -žuγ̇u, Ming 有來) is ‘he was a moderate companion’. I cannot tell whether this is contempt or a plain judgement, and I read it as the first. Shiratori’s closing mark sits on ažuγ̇u; kēġesü ‘when saying’ is the same conditional ending as before, now as a time clause.

sentences.t: Müṅlig ečige uqažu nilbusu aldaγ̇ad ügülerün:
sentences.l: Münlig father perceiving, tear let-fall, saying:
sentences.i: Father Münlig understood, shed tears, and said:
sentences.n: uqažu is uqa- ‘understand, perceive’ (Ming 覺着), which I take as ‘took his meaning’, ‘realised’. Neither the Mongol nor the Ming says what he understood; I guess that it was Teb-Tenggeri’s fate. aldaγ̇ad ‘having let fall’ as in the earlier tears.

sentences.t: "Dair etügen-i taṅlasun-u tedüi büküi-eče

morph.gloss: great (Ming 大), in Dair Etügen ‘Great Earth’ (compare the horse's name Dair) [大]
earth, the earth-goddess Etügen (Ming 地) [(地)行]
clod of earth (Ming 土塊) [土塊 的]
so much; after a genitive, ‘no bigger than’ [那些]

sentences.l: "Great Earth-ACC clod-of so-much being-from,
sentences.i: “Since the time when Mother Etügen, the Great Earth, was no bigger than a clod,
sentences.n: Dair Etügen: etügen is ‘earth’ (Ming 地) and the goddess Etügen (house name, ‘Mother Etügen’), and the Ming reads Dair as 大 ‘great’, so ‘Great Earth’. The glossary has Dair as a horse’s name elsewhere; this is not that word. Taṅlasun-u tedüi, ‘no bigger than a clod of earth’, is the house reading of tedüi after a genitive (Ming 土塊的 那些). büküi-eče is bü- ‘be’ + -küi + the ablative, ‘since it was’ (Ming 有的時行).

sentences.t: dalai müren-i γoroqan-u tedüi büküi-eče nököčebe bi"

morph.gloss: so much; after a genitive, ‘no bigger than’ [那些]
to accompany, be a companion [作伴了]

sentences.l: Sea river-ACC brook-of so-much being-from, accompanied I"
sentences.i: and the sea and the river were no bigger than a brook, I have been your companion.”
sentences.n: Same pattern: dalai müren-i (Ming 海 江行) ‘sea (and) river’, γoroqan-u tedüi ‘no bigger than a brook’, büküi-eče ‘since it was’. nököčebe is nököče- ‘be a companion’ + the past -be (Ming 作伴了), with bi ‘I’. The object ‘your’ is not in the Mongol; the sense is that Münlig has been the Qahan’s companion since the beginning. The closing mark is Shiratori’s, on bi.

sentences.t: keġeküi-lüġe žirγoγ̇an Qoṅγotan köġüd in-ü egüden bosožü

morph.gloss: comitative: at the very moment of
the Qongqotan, a clan name [種(名)]
his, her (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to block, stop up (Ming 塞; stem uncertain) [塞着]

sentences.l: Just-at-the-saying, six Qongqotan sons him-of door blocking,
sentences.i: Just as he said this, his six Qongqotan sons blocked the door,
sentences.n: keġeküi-lüġe is keġe- ‘say’ + the participle -küi + the comitative -lüġe, ‘at the very moment of saying’ (Ming 纔說呵). žirγoγ̇an is ‘six’ (the other sons than Teb-Tenggeri); in-ü is ‘his’ (Münlig’s). bosožü (Ming 塞着 ‘blocking’) has a stem I cannot place.

sentences.t: qolumta toγ̇orin baižu qančud(i)-jan šimaliγaγdarun

morph.gloss: fire-pan, hearth, brazier (Ming 火盤) [火盤]
sleeve (Ming 衣袖; stem inferred) [衣袖(每)自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (back-vowel form, bracketed i)

words.reading: 失馬里中合黑荅舌侖 šimaliγaγdarun

morph.gloss: to roll up the sleeves (stem inferred from the Ming 挽) [被挽時]

sentences.l: Fire-pan around standing, sleeve-own when-rolled,
sentences.i: stood around the fire-pan, and when they rolled up their sleeves,
sentences.n: toγ̇orin ‘around’ (Ming 周圍), baižu ‘standing’. qančud(i)-jan is ‘their own sleeves’ (qanču + the plural -d, then the bracketed i and the reflexive -jan), and šimaliγaγdarun is a verb for rolling up the sleeves, converb of time (-run, ‘when’), with a passive-looking -γaγda- that I cannot explain (Ming 被挽時 ‘when pulled up’).

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan gerelžü siqaγdažu

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
to be afraid (Ming 恐; stem uncertain) [恐着]
to squeeze, press (Ming 擠) [被擠着]

sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan fearing, being-squeezed,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, afraid and hemmed in,
sentences.n: gerelžü is Ming 恐着 ‘fearing’ (stem uncertain); siqaγdažu is siqa- ‘squeeze’ (Ming 擠) + the passive -γda- + -žu, ‘being pressed’. Qaγan is `l`’s form.

sentences.t: "žaila. Γaruja" keġeġed

morph.gloss: sense uncertain (the Ming 𧻞了 contains a character I cannot read; perhaps ‘make way’) [𧻞了]

sentences.l: "žaila. Let-us-go-out," having-said
sentences.i: said, “[žaila]. Let us go out,”
sentences.n: The word žaila I cannot read: the Ming gloss 𧻞了 contains a character I leave as printed, and the word is otherwise unknown to me; perhaps ‘make way’. Γaruja is γar- ‘go out’ + the hortative -uja, ‘let us go out’. Shiratori’s opening mark sits on žaila and his closing mark on Γaruja; `i` supplies ‘said’ before the speech to carry keġeġed.

sentences.t: γarqu-luγ̇a Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-i horčin qorčin turγaγ̇ud toγ̇orin baiba.

words.reading: 中合舌兒中忽-魯阿 γarqu-luγ̇a

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.l: As-soon-as-going-out Chinggis Qaγan-ACC around quiver-bearers day-guards encircling stood.
sentences.i: As soon as they went out, the quiver-bearers and the day guards stood in a ring around Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: γarqu-luγ̇a is γar- ‘go out’ + the participle -qu + -luγ̇a, ‘at the moment of going out’ (Ming 纔出呵). horčin (Ming 周圍) and toγ̇orin (Ming 繞着) both mean ‘around’; qorčin is ‘quiver-bearers’ (house reading) and turγaγ̇ud ‘day guards’ (plural -d, Ming 散班每); baiba ‘stood’. Qaγ̇an-i is the accusative after toγ̇orin, ‘around the Qahan’.

sentences.t: Teb-Teṅgeri-ji terged-ün üžeġür-e niruγ̇u quγulžü oγ̇oruγsan-i Čiṅgis Qaγan üžežü

morph.gloss: cart (terge- before the plural) [車每 的]
tip, end (Ming 捎頭) [捎 行]
to go off (stem uncertain; the Ming 去了的 ‘the one gone’) [去了的行]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.l: Teb-Tenggeri-ACC cart-of tip-at back breaking gone-ACC Chinggis Qaγan seeing,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan saw Teb-Tenggeri, his back broken, who had gone to the tips of the carts,
sentences.n: The object phrase is Teb-Teṅgeri-ji … oγ̇oruγsan-i ‘the one who had gone’ (Ming 去了的行), a past participle from a stem oγ̇or- I cannot place; the Ming 去了 can be a way of saying that someone has died, but it does not say so, and I leave it as ‘gone’. quγulžü and the cart-tips are as above.

sentences.t: qoituγ̇ur-ača nigen boro qošiliγ abčiraγ̇ulžu Teb-Teṅgeri-jin deġere in-ü talbiγ̇ulžu

words.reading: 中豁亦禿兀舌剌察 qoituγ̇ur-ača

morph.gloss: rear, back (Ming 後; formation uncertain) [後行]
tent (Ming 帳房; word uncertain) [帳房]

words.reading: 阿卜赤舌剌兀勒周 abčiraγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: his, her (third-person genitive, set after its noun) [他的]
to set down, let go [敎放]

sentences.l: From-behind one blue-grey tent having-brought, Teb-Tenggeri-of upon his having-set,
sentences.i: and had a blue-grey tent brought from behind and set over Teb-Tenggeri,
sentences.n: qoituγ̇ur-ača is Ming 後行 ‘from behind’, the stem uncertain. nigen boro qošiliγ is ‘one blue-grey tent’ (boro as in the glossary, Ming 靑 ‘blue-green’; qošiliγ, Ming 帳房, is a word I know only from the Ming). abčiraγ̇ulžu is ‘having it brought’ (causative); deġere is ‘above, on top of’; talbiγ̇ulžu ‘having it set down’.

sentences.t: "kölge oroγ̇uludqun; neġüje"

morph.gloss: to yoke, harness a cart (Ming 駕車; as kölgežü, 064–073; here the bare stem, apparently an order; uncertain) [駕車]

words.reading: 斡舌羅兀魯惕中渾 oroγ̇uludqun

sentences.l: "Yoke let-it-be-brought-in; let-us-move-camp"
sentences.i: “Yoke up, and have it brought in; let us move camp.”
sentences.n: kölge (Ming 駕車 ‘to drive / harness a cart’) is the verb kölge- ‘yoke’ that the glossary has in kölgežü and that the earlier parts use of a camel or cart; here it stands as the bare stem, which I take as an order, though I do not know what is to be harnessed. oroγ̇uludqun is oro- ‘enter’ + the causative -γ̇ul- + the polite plural command -dqun (Ming 您), ‘have it brought in’. neġüje is neġü- ‘move camp’ + the hortative -je, ‘let us move camp’. Shiratori’s opening mark sits on kölge and his closing mark on neġüje; the semicolon is his.

sentences.t: keġežü tendēče neġübe.
sentences.l: Saying, from-there moved-camp.
sentences.i: So saying, he moved camp from there.
sentences.n: keġežü ‘saying’ and tendēče ‘from there’ lead to neġübe, neġü- ‘move camp’ + the past -be. The subject, Chinggis Qahan, is carried over from the previous sentences.
